name: HolyMind — Boom boundary stability
reported_issue: Stutter after fireworks end and while scrolling back above Boom.
reproduced_cause: In touch WebKit, height-only viewport changes rebuilt the earlier Assemble pin and changed the page spacer/story geometry. This produced involuntary scroll movement after Boom. This mechanism is verified in simulation; the physical phone cause is not directly observed.

reproduction.input: No native scroll input during the viewport-height perturbation
reproduction.method: Touch-enabled WebKit viewport simulation, not a physical Safari browser-toolbar recording

changes.viewport: Shared stable document-story dimensions ignore small touch height-only/browser-chrome or keyboard changes. Width/orientation changes, substantial resizes and desktop height resizing still rebuild.
changes.pin: The offscreen Assemble pin is not killed/recreated for those transient height changes. Its spacer, document height, instance and downstream Boom range remain stable.
changes.exit: Completed and not-yet-entered fireworks exit before DOM geometry reads; transparent canvas clears only once if needed. No boundary visibility toggle.
changes.frame: Signature geometry is read before continuity style/SVG writes; identical particle frames are not rasterized again, and unchanged decoration values are not rewritten.
changes.native_scroll: No added scroll interception, corrective scrollTo, spacer or new independent animation loop.

preserved.details: Original deterministic outward/inward paths, Mozart order and ringing tails, five firework sounds, +8 dB line-only current, ambient field, brain effects, always-on motion and responsive hero.

live_coverage: After-firework, above-Boom and mid-reverse viewport perturbations; native down/up exits; no geometry reads or paints outside the celebration; identical paused pixels; actual orientation and desktop resize; five rendered reverse-coordinate samples.

limitations.note: This fixes the reproduced scroll jump and redundant boundary rendering. Browser automation is not a guarantee of perceived smoothness or frame rate on the user’s iPhone.
